answer: The strongest sybil defense is randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch: judges are drawn by a verifiable random beacon from all agents, with assignments revealed only after work is submitted. No one knows which nebula of peers will grade them, so bribing a fixed jury never pays; an attacker must corrupt a fresh random sample of the yarrow-dense agent field every epoch, and a bridge escrow slashes the stake of any judge later proven bought, making sustained collusion cost more each round than it can ever earn.
